messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test triggers an infinite loop when HelpFormatter tries to print a help message option with a very long word that doesn't fit within the specified width (20 characters in the test). The core of the issue lies in the method HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(StringBuffer sb, int width, int nextLineTabStop, String text).

The code attempts to wrap the given text to the specified width by repeatedly calling findWrapPos to find a suitable wrap position. If findWrapPos returns -1, it means no wrapping is needed, so the text is appended as is and the method returns normally.

However, if the wrap position (pos) returned by findWrapPos does not advance compared to the last position (lastPos), this means no progress is made in splitting the text. This indicates the word is too long to fit in one line but cannot be wrapped properly. The code then throws a RuntimeException stating "Text too long for line - throwing exception to avoid infinite loop [CLI-162]".

According to the bug report however, the formatter used to hang and crash with OutOfMemoryError instead of throwing this exception. This suggests that before this RuntimeException was introduced, the code would go into an endless loop at this part. The exception was probably introduced to prevent the infinite loop problem.

The test case calls printHelp which eventually calls printOptions and then renderOptions, which calls renderWrappedText to wrap option descriptions. When the description has one long word longer than the width, findWrapPos will struggle to find wrapping points, leading to the infinite loop or exception.

In summary, the bug arises because of improper handling of very long words in the wrapping logic of renderWrappedText. With the current code snippet, the RuntimeException prevents infinite loops but if this check was missing the loop would never break, causing hangs and OutOfMemoryError.

Next, we should verify details of findWrapPos method to see how it detect wrapping positions and why it fails on very long words.

messages.content:
The method findWrapPos works as follows:
- If a newline or tab character occurs before the width limit, it returns that position+1.
- If the remaining text is shorter than the width, it returns -1 (no wrap needed).
- Otherwise, it tries to find the last whitespace character before startPos+width to wrap there.
- If no whitespace exists before that position, it searches forwards after startPos+width for the first whitespace character and returns it.
- If still no whitespace is found and the search reaches the end, it returns -1.

On very long words without whitespace, the backward search will fail, and the forward search will advance pos until the end of the text (pos == text.length()), causing findWrapPos to return -1. If this happens during wrapping in renderWrappedText, then wrapping finishes normally.

The infinite loop problem would occur if the wrapping code never makes progress in the substring it uses in each loop iteration, i.e., the wrap position does not advance (pos == lastPos), causing the method to run forever appending the same text repeatedly.

The fix was to throw an exception (RuntimeException) to prevent this infinite loop.

Summary:
- The root cause is that when the text contains a very long unbreakable word, the current wrapping algorithm either fails to wrap or doesn't advance position.
- The bug report describes the problem before the addition of the RuntimeException check.
- The exception was introduced to stop infinite looping by detecting zero-progress wrapping and explicitly throwing.

Therefore, the infinite loop was caused by renderWrappedText not properly exiting if the text is too long to break and would repeat the same substring wrapping infinitely. The check at line 834-836 throws an explicit RuntimeException to prevent infinite loop, but the old behavior without this would hang and eventually cause the JVM to crash.

This explains the infinite loop crash on long words during HelpFormatter.printHelp with small width settings.

The most relevant code to fix or improve would be in HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText and possibly also findWrapPos if we want smarter break logic for long words.

No other recent bug reports seemed relevant to this specific infinite loop problem.
